quickSummary: Small cations with high charge density (Li⁺) exhibit massive hydration enthalpies, binding huge water shells that reduce their aqueous ionic mobility: Mobility follows Cs⁺(aq) > Rb⁺(aq) > K⁺(aq) > Na⁺(aq) > Li⁺(aq).
summary: Master the inverse relationship between hydration enthalpy and aqueous ionic mobility for alkali and alkaline earth cations.

summaryBox.takeaway: s-Block (ns¹⁻²): Highly electropositive metals; p-Block (ns² np¹⁻⁶): Metals, metalloids, non-metals, halogens, noble gases.

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **s-Block (Groups 1 & 2)**: Outer configuration $ns^{1-2}$ (Alkali metals and Alkaline earth metals). Highly reactive, low IE, form ionic compounds.
• **p-Block (Groups 13–18)**: Outer configuration $ns^2 np^{1-6}$. Encompasses metals, metalloids, non-metals, halogens, and noble gases.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Hydration Enthalpy vs Aqueous Ionic Mobility
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Hydration Enthalpy vs Aqueous Ionic Mobility
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GROUP 1 HYDRATION vs MOBILITY
                       
   Gaseous Ionic Radii:           Li⁺ < Na⁺ < K⁺ < Rb⁺ < Cs⁺
   Hydration Enthalpy (Δ_hyd H):  Li⁺ > Na⁺ > K⁺ > Rb⁺ > Cs⁺
   Hydrated Ionic Radii (aq):     Li⁺(aq) > Na⁺(aq) > K⁺(aq) > Rb⁺(aq) > Cs⁺(aq)
   Aqueous Ionic Mobility:        Cs⁺(aq) > Rb⁺(aq) > K⁺(aq) > Na⁺(aq) > Li⁺(aq)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Hydration enthalpy is the exothermic energy released when $1\text{ mole}$ of gaseous ions undergoes complete hydration:

$$\mathbf{\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H \propto \text{Charge Density} \propto \frac{z^2}{r}}$$

• **Physiological Cause**: $\text{Li}^+$ has the smallest gaseous ionic radius and highest charge density, binding a giant, thick sphere of water molecules. Thus, $\text{Li}^+(\text{aq})$ has the largest hydrodynamic hydrated radius, experiences maximum viscous drag, and displays the **LOWEST aqueous ionic mobility** and electrical conductance.

quickRevision: Gaseous radius: Li⁺ < Na⁺ < K⁺ < Rb⁺ < Cs⁺.
Hydrated radius: Li⁺(aq) > Na⁺(aq) > K⁺(aq) > Rb⁺(aq) > Cs⁺(aq).
Aqueous mobility: Cs⁺(aq) > Rb⁺(aq) > K⁺(aq) > Na⁺(aq) > Li⁺(aq).
